blocks.html:
What to know

  • Monosaccharides are simple sugars. Glucose is the main fuel; fructose and galactose are converted to glucose or glycolytic intermediates in the liver.
  • Disaccharides are two sugars. Sucrose is glucose + fructose, lactose is glucose + galactose, and maltose is two glucose units. Lactase splits lactose; its loss causes lactose intolerance.
  • Polysaccharides store or structure. Glycogen is the branched animal store; starch is the plant store; cellulose is indigestible fiber that adds bulk and feeds gut bacteria.
  • Glycoproteins and glycolipids decorate membranes. Sugar chains help cells recognize each other, form blood-group antigens, and clear glycoproteins from the blood.
  • GLUT transporters move glucose. GLUT4 responds to insulin in muscle and fat; GLUT1 supplies the brain and red cells; GLUT2 in liver and pancreas senses glucose.

Check

check.question: Which carbohydrate is the main storage form of glucose in human liver and muscle?
check.explanation: Glycogen is the branched glucose polymer stored in liver and muscle. Starch is the plant store; cellulose is fiber.
